decision-trees-in-machine-learning-and-d.subtitle: A Visual Infographic Guide from Entropy and Gini to Python, Pruning, and Interpretable AI
decision-trees-in-machine-learning-and-d.seo_description: A 136-page visual guide to decision trees covering tree anatomy, entropy, Gini impurity, information gain, CART, ID3, C4.5, pruning, scikit-learn, real-world projects, interviews, and interpretable AI.
decision-trees-in-machine-learning-and-d.summary:
Decision Trees in Machine Learning and Data Science is a 136-page visual learning system that turns one of machine learning’s most interpretable model families into a sequence of diagrams, formulas, worked examples, code panels, projects, warnings, interview questions, and quick-reference pages. It begins with the core intuition that a decision tree is a learned hierarchy of useful questions. From there, the reader moves through supervised-learning context, classification versus regression, interpretability and limitations, then into the anatomy of roots, internal nodes, branches, leaves, decision paths, thresholds, depth, and binary or multi-way splits.

The mathematical core explains how a tree decides where to split. Impurity, entropy, information gain, Gini impurity, weighted impurity, regression error measures, and split selection are developed visually before the book moves into recursive partitioning, greedy learning, ID3, C4.5, CART, stopping criteria, overfitting, bias–variance trade-offs, validation, class imbalance, sample weighting, leakage, and pruning. Cost-complexity pruning and model control are treated not as optional cleanup but as part of the discipline required to keep a tree useful beyond the training data.

The final third converts the theory into practice with Python and scikit-learn workflows for classifiers and regressors, encoding, visualization, metrics, model inspection, and GridSearchCV. Real-world projects span classic and applied problems such as Play Tennis, Titanic survival, churn, credit decisions, car evaluation, heart-disease examples, factory scenarios, weather, and house prices, with educational and ethical cautions where the domain requires them. Interview questions, common mistakes, formula references, a visual glossary, and a final concept map connect the entire journey from data to questions, splits, impurity, algorithms, pruning, Python, projects, interpretation, and interpretable AI.
learning: Explain a decision tree as a hierarchy of learned questions rather than a random sequence of hand-written rules.
Distinguish classification trees from regression trees and understand the different objectives they optimize.
Read roots, internal nodes, branches, leaves, thresholds, paths, depth, samples, values, classes, and rules in a trained tree.
Calculate and interpret entropy, information gain, Gini impurity, weighted impurity, and regression error criteria.
Understand greedy recursive partitioning and the practical roles of ID3, C4.5, and CART.
Recognize overfitting, bias–variance trade-offs, data leakage, imbalance, and the role of stopping criteria.
Use pre-pruning and cost-complexity pruning to control tree complexity and improve generalization discipline.
Build, visualize, inspect, and tune DecisionTreeClassifier and DecisionTreeRegressor workflows with scikit-learn.
Apply tree reasoning to multiple real-world project patterns while keeping interpretability and domain limitations visible.
Prepare for interviews with common questions, mistakes, formulas, visual reference material, and explainable model reasoning.
decision-trees-in-machine-learning-and-d.target_audience: For students, data analysts, aspiring data scientists, machine-learning practitioners, Python learners, interview candidates, and visual learners who want to understand decision trees from intuition and mathematics through implementation, model control, projects, and interpretable AI.

sql-for-data-analysis.subtitle: A Visual, Practical Guide with Real Business Projects, Interview Problems, CTEs, Window Functions, Dashboards, and Portfolio Workflows
sql-for-data-analysis.seo_description: A comprehensive visual SQL guide spanning relational foundations, schema design, SELECT, joins, aggregation, CTEs, window functions, dialect differences, interviews, business projects, optimization, dashboards, and portfolio delivery.
sql-for-data-analysis.summary:
SQL for Data Analysis is a large visual, practice-oriented journey from the first relational concepts to advanced analytical work and portfolio delivery. Its learning architecture spans eighteen parts and treats SQL as more than syntax: the reader learns how data is structured, how table grain affects meaning, how databases and schemas are designed, how analysts work inside SQL tools and workspaces, and how command families, CRUD operations, data types, table creation, imports, exports, constraints, keys, NULL behavior, DDL, DML, and transactions fit into a reliable analytical workflow.

The central analysis sections develop clean SELECT queries, filtering, Boolean logic, sorting, date work, aggregation, GROUP BY, HAVING, descriptive statistics, joins, set operators, multi-table analysis, functions, CASE expressions, and data cleaning before moving into reusable logic with subqueries, CTEs, views, and temporary structures. Window functions receive a dedicated advanced section covering partitions, ordering, frames, ranking, running metrics, FIRST_VALUE, LAST_VALUE, PERCENT_RANK, CUME_DIST, ROW_NUMBER, and related analytical patterns while preserving row-level detail. Throughout the book, examples use realistic sample tables, show query-to-output relationships, identify common traps, and distinguish business meaning from implementation detail.

A defining feature of the book is its dialect-aware and safety-aware approach. Portable principles are separated from engine-specific behavior across PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQL Server, SQLite, and GoogleSQL for BigQuery when syntax or semantics differ. Destructive operations are treated with preview, validation, transaction, and rollback discipline rather than casual copy-and-run instructions. The final sections turn knowledge into performance through SQL interview patterns, structured problem solving, real business questions, optimization, dashboard-oriented thinking, portfolio projects, and a thirty-day practice and career-delivery plan. The result is a visual reference for learning to query, validate, interpret, and apply data—not merely memorize commands.
learning: Understand relational data, table grain, database structure, schemas, keys, constraints, and data integrity before writing analysis queries.
Create and query tables using appropriate data types, CRUD operations, imports, exports, and safe transaction workflows.
Write clear SELECT queries with filtering, logic, sorting, dates, NULL handling, and reproducible exploratory patterns.
Use aggregation, GROUP BY, HAVING, and statistics without accidentally changing analytical grain or double-counting data.
Combine tables with joins and set operators while detecting multiplicity, unmatched rows, duplicates, and other common analysis traps.
Clean and transform data with functions, CASE expressions, reusable subqueries, CTEs, views, and temporary logic.
Apply window functions for ranking, sequences, running metrics, relative comparisons, distributions, and frame-aware analysis.
Recognize important SQL dialect differences across PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQL Server, SQLite, and GoogleSQL for BigQuery.
Solve interview-style SQL problems by defining the business question, validating intermediate results, and explaining the reasoning.
Turn SQL work into business-facing projects, dashboards, optimized workflows, portfolio evidence, and a structured practice plan.
sql-for-data-analysis.target_audience: For aspiring and working data analysts, data-science learners, BI professionals, students, career switchers, SQL interview candidates, and anyone who wants a visual path from database fundamentals to advanced analytics, business projects, and portfolio-ready work.

weather-air-quality-and-extreme-heat-at-.seo_description: A 100-page visual home guide to extreme heat, thermal comfort, shading, ventilation, fans, air conditioning, smoke and PM2.5, indoor air quality, cooling costs, power outages, and practical heat-safe household decisions.
weather-air-quality-and-extreme-heat-at-.summary:
Weather, Air Quality and Extreme Heat at Home is a 100-page visual handbook built around one practical idea: a home is a connected heat-and-air system, not a collection of unrelated devices. The book begins by showing how heat enters, is generated, is stored, moves through materials and air, and eventually must leave. Radiation, conduction, convection, thermal mass, humidity, air movement, hot nights, urban heat islands, and the microclimate outside a particular window are translated into household-scale diagrams so readers can diagnose why a room or dwelling becomes uncomfortable before buying a solution.

The middle of the book turns diagnosis into layered action. It examines window orientation and glass, roofs, walls, insulation, thermal bridges, leakage, room layout, internal heat sources, balconies and top-floor conditions, then develops a shade-first strategy using external shading, interior blinds and curtains, solar-control films, reflective surfaces, trees, cool roofs, and rental-friendly measures. Ventilation is treated as a decision rather than a ritual: cross-ventilation, single-sided ventilation, stack effect, night flushing, fan placement, ceiling fans, evaporative cooling, dehumidification, zone cooling, air-conditioning types and sizing, thermostat strategy, portable units, maintenance, and smart controls are compared according to context.

Heat is only half the indoor-environment problem, so the later pages connect cooling to air quality and energy. The book covers outdoor pollution, PM2.5, wildfire smoke, the trade-off between opening windows for cooling and closing them for cleaner air, air purifiers, clean-air rooms, CO₂ as a ventilation clue, cooking particles and moisture, condensation and mold risk, electricity bills, cooling demand, cost-versus-impact decisions, and power-outage strategies. Illustrative household scenarios—including Mediterranean and humid coastal homes—show how the pieces interact, and the final action planning converts the whole system into a practical 24-hour routine that changes with sun, temperature, humidity, air quality, and household needs.
learning: Read a home as a heat-and-air system and identify how radiation, conduction, convection, internal gains, storage, and leakage interact.
Build a simple home heat profile using orientation, windows, roof, walls, insulation, layout, occupancy, and local microclimate.
Prioritize shading and solar control before relying only on mechanical cooling.
Decide when ventilation can help by comparing indoor and outdoor temperature, humidity, air quality, wind, noise, security, and time of day.
Use cross-ventilation, night flushing, fans, ceiling fans, zone cooling, and other low-energy strategies in the right context.
Understand the roles and limitations of evaporative cooling, dehumidification, portable air conditioners, and correctly sized cooling systems.
Balance heat relief with PM2.5, wildfire smoke, outdoor pollution, filtration, and clean-air-room strategies.
Use CO₂ as a ventilation clue without treating it as a universal measure of every indoor pollutant.
Connect cooling choices to electricity use, maintenance, cost, resilience, and power-outage planning.
Create a 24-hour household heat plan that changes as conditions change rather than following one fixed rule.
weather-air-quality-and-extreme-heat-at-.target_audience: For renters and homeowners, apartment residents, households facing hot summers or heat waves, people balancing cooling with indoor-air concerns, and non-specialist readers who want a practical visual framework for making their home cooler, cleaner, and more energy-aware without assuming one solution fits every building or climate.

espana-ante-el-calor.category: Hogar, clima y calidad del aire
espana-ante-el-calor.subtitle: Guía visual para una vivienda fresca, saludable y eficiente
espana-ante-el-calor.seo_description: Guía visual de 100 páginas para afrontar el calor en viviendas de España: sombra, ventilación, persianas, toldos, refrigeración, humedad, calima, humo, calidad del aire, consumo energético y decisiones adaptadas al clima.
espana-ante-el-calor.summary:
España ante el calor es una guía visual de 100 páginas concebida específicamente para viviendas, climas y rutinas de España. No es una traducción literal de una guía internacional: reconstruye la lógica térmica y de calidad del aire con terminología de España, unidades métricas, euros cuando son necesarios, pisos, áticos, patios, balcones, persianas, toldos y situaciones reales de vivienda. El recorrido parte de una idea sencilla pero decisiva: la casa funciona como un sistema térmico. El calor entra, se genera, se almacena, se desplaza y debe salir; por eso comprender radiación, conducción, convección, inercia térmica, humedad, movimiento del aire, noches tropicales, isla de calor urbana y microclima permite elegir mejor antes de gastar dinero en una solución.

La parte práctica enseña a construir el perfil térmico de la vivienda y a leer orientación, recorrido solar, ventanas, vidrio, cubierta, fachadas, aislamiento, puentes térmicos, infiltraciones, distribución interior y fuentes de calor. A partir de ese diagnóstico se desarrolla una estrategia por capas: primero controlar la ganancia solar con sombra exterior, toldos, persianas, cortinas, películas solares, superficies adecuadas y soluciones compatibles con viviendas de alquiler; después decidir cuándo abrir o cerrar, cómo aprovechar ventilación cruzada, ventilación nocturna, ventiladores, deshumidificación, refrigeración por zonas y aire acondicionado sin convertir una regla útil en una receta universal. El libro rota deliberadamente entre calor seco del interior, calor extremo andaluz, humedad mediterránea, humedad atlántica y noches muy cálidas.

La guía también integra un problema que a menudo se separa del calor: la calidad del aire. Explica cómo decidir entre ventilar para refrescar o cerrar frente a contaminación, PM2,5, PM10, calima, polvo sahariano o humo de incendios; aborda purificadores, caudal de aire limpio, una habitación prioritaria de aire limpio, CO₂ como pista de ventilación y el efecto de cocinar sobre partículas, humedad y temperatura. Las últimas páginas conectan confort, factura eléctrica, demanda de refrigeración, mantenimiento, cortes de suministro y planificación diaria. El objetivo no es imponer una temperatura o un aparato, sino dar al lector un sistema visual para observar su vivienda, comparar condiciones y tomar decisiones más frescas, saludables y eficientes según su clima y su edificio.
learning: Entender la vivienda como un sistema conectado de calor, aire, humedad y almacenamiento térmico.
Reconocer cómo radiación, conducción, convección, infiltraciones y fuentes internas contribuyen al sobrecalentamiento.
Construir un perfil térmico básico de la vivienda antes de elegir medidas de refrigeración.
Priorizar sombra, persianas, toldos y control solar según orientación, ventanas, cubierta y fachada.
Decidir cuándo abrir o cerrar ventanas comparando temperatura, humedad, calidad del aire, viento, ruido, seguridad y hora del día.
Combinar ventilación cruzada, ventilación nocturna, ventiladores, deshumidificación y refrigeración mecánica según el contexto.
Adaptar decisiones a calor seco interior, calor andaluz, humedad mediterránea o atlántica y noches tropicales.
Responder a calima, polvo sahariano, contaminación y humo equilibrando refrigeración, ventilación y filtración.
Relacionar tamaño de estancia, filtración, caudal de aire limpio, ubicación, ruido y mantenimiento de purificadores.
Conectar confort térmico con consumo, factura eléctrica, mantenimiento, resiliencia y un plan diario adaptable.
espana-ante-el-calor.target_audience: Para personas que viven en España —en pisos, áticos, viviendas interiores, casas costeras o viviendas en zonas de calor seco— y quieren comprender por qué se sobrecalienta su hogar, cómo combinar sombra, ventilación y refrigeración, y cómo proteger simultáneamente el confort, la calidad del aire y el consumo energético.
